title: TimeBank Prepaid Hours and the Rate Discount on Professional Services Projects
content:
The prepaid-hours component of the rate discount locked at signature on a Professional Services Projects time-and-materials statement of work rests on the TimeBank Prepaid Service Hours granted to the client.

## Clause

The prepaid-hours component of the rate discount locked at signature rests on the TimeBank hours granted to the client across all its TimeBank blocks in the twelve months before the signature date; a grant counts when fewer than twelve whole months separate its entry date from the signature date, a whole month being complete only on the same day number of a later month. A client granted 80 hours or more earns the flat 1.5 percentage points; a client granted fewer than 80 but more than zero hours earns 1.5 multiplied by its granted hours and divided by 80, rounded down to one decimal place; a client granted no hours earns nothing.

| Hours granted in the window | Prepaid-hours component |
|---|---|
| 80 or more | 1.5, whatever the hours above 80 |
| more than zero, fewer than 80 | 1.5 multiplied by the granted hours, divided by 80, rounded down to one decimal place |
| none | nothing |

The hours read are the grant entries on the hours ledgers of the client's TimeBank blocks; draws, reversals, rollovers and forfeitures are not grants.

## Worked examples (hypothetical figures)

- 120 hours granted: 1.5.
- 40 hours granted: 1.5 multiplied by 40 and divided by 80 is 0.75, rounded down to 0.7.
- 79 hours granted: 1.5 multiplied by 79 and divided by 80 is 1.48125, rounded down to 1.4.

## Window boundary (hypothetical dates)

A grant entered on 15 March of one year counts toward a signature on 14 March of the next year (eleven whole months have passed) and does not count toward a signature on 15 March of the next year (twelve whole months have passed). A grant entered on the 31st of a month completes a whole month only on the 31st of a later month.
